paragraphs.source_en: Eight days after my graduation, the principal of the college sent for me. I was asked if I would go as a teacher of mathematics with a salary of forty yen per month to a certain middle school in Shikoku. It is true that I had spent three long years in learning, yet had no intention of being a teacher, or going into the country. However, indecision is what I dislike most, and I answered on the spot that I would accept the offer. This of course came partly from the lack of positions in view, except that of teacher, but the hereditary rashness was again at the bottom of the mistake.
